newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Australian bonds waiting on FOMC, wages.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Australian bonds waiting on FOMC, wages.

text.p: *Bonds come off slightly in SYCOM as Treasuries soften ahead of the FOMC meeting. Analysts appear divided on whether an interest rate hike will follow.
*Local bonds also have wage figures on Wednesday and Thursday to provide some solid direction.

Australian bonds eased a notch in the SYCOM session as the U.S. market was softer in the final session ahead of the Federal Reserve's FOMC meeting, with the local market also waiting on key wages data for direction.
After pulling back from 12-week highs in Friday's SYCOM session, bonds have held to narrow ranges and are expected to stay that way in the local session on Tuesday.

The U.S. market, and consquently Australian bonds, have benefitted from growing sentiment that the FOMC will leave rates on hold at this meeting, although analysts are fairly evenly divided on the prospects for policy.
Some felt the market had become too optimistic, and left themselves open to be caught out if the Fed did move.

"In contrast to the lead-up to the March 25 decision by the Fed policymakers... U.S. bond and equities markets appear to be ill-prepared for a further rise in rates at this Tuesday's FOMC meeting," Macquarie Bank economists said.
Local markets also have two sets of key wages data to be released in coming days that are seen as key to the interest rate outlook, and so should also help keep trading on Tuesday confined to ranges.

Wednesday sees the expected release of Department of Industrial Relation data on enterprise bargaining agreements (EBA) for the March quarter, while final first quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings data (AWOTE) is due on Thursday.

With wages seen as a key obstacle to hopes of another rate cut, signs of acceleration in EBAs or private sector AWOTE would weaken the market, and possibly see a tightening begin to be aggressively factored into the bill market for later this year.
